title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Revised Regulations on the Supervision Work of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Revised "People's Court Supervision Work Regulations"

Fa Fa [2013] No. 3

All local people's courts at various levels, military courts at various levels, intermediate and basic people's courts for railway transport, maritime courts, and people's courts of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The revised "People's Court Supervision Work Regulations" are hereby issued to you for conscientious implementation.

January 31, 2013

People's Court Supervision Work Regulations

(Issued on June 5, 2008, revised on January 31, 2013)

Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the "Public Servant Law of the People's Republic of China", the "Judges Law of the People's Republic of China", and other laws, and with reference to the "Administrative Supervision Law of the People's Republic of China", in order to strengthen the supervision work of the people's courts, enforce the discipline of the people's courts, promote the construction of integrity, and safeguard judicial justice.

Article 2 The supervision department of a people's court is a specialized body exercising the supervisory function of the people's court, and it supervises the people's court and its judges and other staff in accordance with the law and these Regulations.

Article 3 The supervision department of a people's court shall exercise its powers in accordance with the law and these Regulations, and shall not be subject to interference from administrative organs, social organizations, individuals, or other departments within the people's court.

Article 4 The supervision work of the people's courts must adhere to the principle of seeking truth from facts, focusing on evidence and investigation, and ensuring equality for everyone in the application of law and discipline.

Article 5 The supervision work of the people's courts shall combine education with punishment, strictly enforce discipline while safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of judges and other staff, and integrate supervision and inspection with the improvement of systems and work methods.

Article 6 The supervision work of the people's courts shall rely on the masses. The supervision department shall establish a reporting system. Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations have the right to lodge complaints or reports with the supervision department against the disciplinary or illegal acts of the people's courts and their judges and other staff.

Chapter 2 Supervision Departments and Supervisory Personnel

Article 7 The Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts shall establish Supervision Bureaus. The Intermediate People's Courts shall establish Supervision Divisions.

Basic People's Courts with 60 or more staff shall establish Supervision Sections; those with 30 or more but less than 60 staff shall have full-time supervisors; those with less than 30 staff shall have part-time supervisors.

Article 8 The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court, under the leadership of the President of the Supreme People's Court, shall be responsible for the supervision work of the courts nationwide.

The supervision departments of local people's courts at various levels and the full-time or part-time supervisors of basic people's courts shall carry out their work under the leadership of the president of their own court and the supervision department of the higher-level court, with the supervision business being primarily directed by the supervision department of the higher-level court.

Article 9 The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts shall have one Director and one to three Deputy Directors; the Supervision Division (Section) of the Intermediate and Basic People's Courts shall have one Division (Section) Chief and one to two Deputy Division (Section) Chiefs.

The responsible persons of the supervision departments of people's courts at various levels shall generally be selected and appointed from among judges or persons qualified to be judges.

The appointment and removal of the responsible persons of the supervision departments of local people's courts at various levels and the full-time or part-time supervisors of basic people's courts shall be subject to the consent of the supervision department of the next higher-level people's court before it is decided.

Article 10 The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts may establish internal organs according to work needs, responsible for handling letters and visits and reports, investigation and handling of cases, supervision and inspection, trial supervision, comprehensive research, etc. Intermediate People's Courts may refer to this and establish such organs according to work needs.

Article 11 The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court may have bureau-level supervisory commissioners; the Supervision Bureaus of High People's Courts and the Supervision Divisions of Intermediate People's Courts in municipalities directly under the Central Government and sub-provincial cities may have division-level supervisory commissioners; the Supervision Divisions of other Intermediate People's Courts may have section-level supervisory commissioners.

Full-time supervisors of Basic People's Courts shall be appointed at the level equivalent to the principal head of a department within the court; part-time supervisors shall be held by deputy leaders at the court level.

People's courts at all levels shall, as far as possible, select judges or persons qualified to be judges to serve as supervisory commissioners or full-time supervisors.

People's courts at all levels shall select full-time or part-time integrity supervisors in their trial, enforcement, and other departments. Full-time integrity supervisors shall be senior judges with non-leading positions equivalent to the principal or deputy principal head of a department and other personnel familiar with department work; part-time integrity supervisors shall be concurrently held by deputy heads of the department.

Full-time or part-time integrity supervisors shall carry out their work under the leadership of the principal responsible person of their department and the supervision department of their court.

Article 12 Supervisory personnel must be loyal to their duties, enforce discipline impartially, abide by laws and discipline, and maintain confidentiality.

Article 13 Where supervisory personnel abuse their power, engage in malpractices for personal gain, neglect their duties, or disclose secrets, they shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions; if the conduct constitutes a crime, they shall be transferred to the relevant authorities for handling according to law.

Chapter 3 Duties of the Supervision Department

Article 14 The main duties of the supervision department of a people's court are:

(1) To inspect the compliance of the people's court and its judges and other staff with national laws and regulations;

(2) To formulate and improve the integrity system of the people's court, and inspect the implementation of the integrity system by the people's court and its judges and other staff;

(3) To accept complaints and reports against disciplinary or illegal acts of the people's court and its judges and other staff;

(4) To investigate and handle acts of the people's court and its judges and other staff that violate trial discipline, enforcement discipline, or other discipline;

(5) To accept reviews and appeals of judges and other staff against disciplinary sanctions;

(6) To organize, coordinate, inspect, guide, supervise, and rectify improper practices of the people's court and its judges and other staff that harm the interests of the masses and damage judicial credibility;

(7) To organize, coordinate, inspect, and guide corruption prevention work, and carry out education on judicial integrity and compliance with laws and discipline for judges and other staff.

Article 15 The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court shall supervise the following units, departments, and personnel:

(1) The departments of the Supreme People's Court and their judges and other staff;

(2) The High People's Courts and their presidents, vice-presidents, court-level leading cadres, and Directors of the Supervision Bureau.

Article 16 The Supervision Bureaus of High People's Courts and the Supervision Divisions of Intermediate People's Courts shall supervise the following units, departments, and personnel:

(1) The departments of their own court and their judges and other staff;

(2) The next lower-level people's courts and their presidents, vice-presidents, court-level leading cadres, principal responsible persons of the supervision departments, or full-time supervisors.

Article 17 The Supervision Sections or full-time or part-time supervisors of Basic People's Courts shall supervise the departments of their own court and their judges and other staff.

Article 18 The supervision department of a higher-level people's court may handle supervisory matters within the jurisdiction of the supervision department of a lower-level people's court; when necessary, it may handle supervisory matters within the jurisdiction of the supervision departments of all people's courts under its jurisdiction.

Chapter 4 Powers of the Supervision Department

Article 19 When performing its duties, the supervision department has the power to require the supervised units, departments, and personnel to provide documents, materials, case files, financial accounts, and other relevant materials related to the supervisory matter, and to inspect or copy them; it has the power to require the supervised units, departments, and personnel to make explanations or clarifications regarding issues involved in the supervisory matter; it has the power to order the supervised units, departments, and personnel to cease acts that violate laws, regulations, and discipline.

Article 20 When investigating acts that violate laws, regulations, and discipline, the supervision department may take the following measures according to the actual circumstances:

(1) Temporarily seize or seal up documents, materials, financial accounts, case materials, and other relevant materials of the units, departments, and personnel involved in the case that may prove acts violating laws, regulations, and discipline;

(2) Order the relevant units, departments, and personnel involved in the case not to sell, transfer, or destroy property related to the case during the investigation;

(3) With the approval of the supervision department of the next higher-level people's court, order persons suspected of violating discipline to explain and clarify issues related to the investigation at a specified time and place, but may not detain them or impose disguised detention;

(4) Recommend suspending persons with serious suspicion of violating discipline from performing official duties;

(5) With approval, inquire into the deposits of the units and persons involved in the case at banks or other financial institutions, and if necessary, may take preservation measures according to law to freeze the deposits of the persons involved in the case at banks or other financial institutions;

(6) Make inquiries to the units, departments, and personnel involved in the supervisory matter;

(7) Attend meetings of the supervised units or departments related to the supervisory matter.

When taking the measures specified in items (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) of the preceding paragraph, a notice of supervision shall be prepared and served on the relevant units, departments, and personnel, and a list of the relevant property shall be made.

Article 21 Based on the results of inspections or investigations, the supervision department may make supervision recommendations under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Where laws or regulations are refused to be implemented or are violated, or where the discipline of the people's court is violated, and correction is necessary;

(2) Where the discipline of the people's court is violated, and sanctions such as warning, demerit, serious demerit, rank reduction, removal from office, or dismissal are warranted;

(3) Where decisions on recruitment, appointment and removal, or rewards and punishments are clearly inappropriate and correction is necessary;

(4) Where systems need to be improved to close loopholes;

(5) Other circumstances where a supervision recommendation is necessary.

Article 22 Supervision recommendations shall be issued in the name of the people's court and served in writing on the relevant units, departments, and personnel.

Important supervision recommendations shall be reported to the supervision department of the next higher-level people's court for filing.

The relevant units, departments, and personnel shall adopt the supervision recommendations; if they object to a supervision recommendation, they shall submit a written objection to the people's court that made the recommendation within 30 days from the date of receipt of the recommendation. The supervision department shall respond within 30 days from the date of receipt of the objection.

Article 23 Based on the results of inspections or investigations, where a person who violates the discipline of the people's court should be subject to disciplinary sanctions, the supervision department shall propose a disciplinary sanction opinion or make a supervision recommendation in accordance with the disciplinary sanction procedures.

Chapter 5 Supervision Procedures

Article 24 The supervision department shall conduct inspections according to the following procedures:

(1) Determine the inspection matter based on the instructions or requirements of the president of the court or the supervision department of the higher-level people's court;

(2) Formulate an inspection plan and organize its implementation; when necessary, relevant departments of the court or lower-level people's courts may be organized to participate in the inspection;

(3) Report the inspection results to the president of the court or the supervision department of the higher-level people's court;

(4) Based on the inspection results, propose disciplinary sanction opinions or supervision recommendations.

Article 25 Where, based on the scope of jurisdiction and problems discovered during inspections, or clues of disciplinary violations from complaints or reports, or clues of disciplinary violations transferred by relevant authorities or departments, and after preliminary verification, the supervision department considers that a person has committed a violation and should be given disciplinary sanctions, it shall report to the president of the court for approval before filing a case and organizing an investigation.

The filing of important cases shall be reported to the supervision department of the next higher-level people's court for filing.

Article 26 When investigating disciplinary cases, the supervision department of a people's court shall form a case investigation team and a case adjudication team to conduct the case investigation and case adjudication separately. Personnel participating in the case investigation shall not participate in the case adjudication.

If the personnel of the supervision department are insufficient to form a case investigation team and a case adjudication team, the supervision department may, with the approval of the supervising court leader in charge, transfer personnel from other departments of the court or from the supervision department of a lower-level people's court to participate in the case investigation and case adjudication.

Article 27 When investigating a disciplinary case, the supervision department shall collect evidence comprehensively and hear the statements and defenses of the person under investigation.

Article 28 Where a supervisory officer has an interest in the supervisory matter being handled, or has other relationships that may affect the fair handling of the case, that supervisory officer shall recuse himself or herself.

Article 29 A case investigated upon filing by the supervision department shall be concluded within six months from the date of filing. If an extension is necessary due to special reasons, the period may be appropriately extended, but the matter shall be reported to the supervision department of the next higher-level people's court for filing, with an explanation of the circumstances and reasons.

Article 30 For a case investigated upon filing, if it is determined through investigation that the disciplinary violation does not exist, or the circumstances are minor and do not require disciplinary sanctions, the case shall be dismissed in accordance with the procedures for filing, and the person under investigation shall be informed.

Article 31 For a case that may result in disciplinary sanctions, after the investigation team concludes the investigation, the case shall be referred to the adjudication team for adjudication.

Article 32 Adjudication of cases shall be conducted by way of a hearing or in writing. When adjudicating a case in writing, the person under investigation shall be questioned and their statements and defenses heard; when necessary, the testimony may also be verified with witnesses.

Article 33 Disciplinary sanctions against a person who violates discipline shall be imposed in accordance with the following provisions:

(1) For a member of the Adjudication Committee, division head, deputy division head, judge, assistant judge, or other staff of the court, or the president, vice-president, court-level leading cadre, principal responsible person of the supervision department, or full-time supervisor of a lower-level people's court, if a warning, demerit, or serious demerit is to be imposed, the supervision department shall propose a sanction opinion, report it to the president of the court for approval, and then issue a decision on disciplinary sanction; if rank reduction, removal from office, or dismissal is to be imposed, the supervision department shall propose a sanction opinion, and after approval by the president's office meeting of the court, issue a decision on disciplinary sanction. The decision on disciplinary sanction shall be issued in the name of the people's court and affixed with the seal of the people's court.

(2) If a sanction of removal from office or dismissal is to be imposed on a person who violates discipline, and it is necessary to first request the people's congress at the corresponding level to recall the position, or to request the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level to remove the position or cancel the position, the sanction decision shall be executed only after the people's congress or its standing committee has recalled, removed, or cancelled the position.

Article 34 After a disciplinary sanction is imposed on a person who violates discipline, the personnel department of the relevant court shall go through the procedures for the sanction, and the decision on disciplinary sanction and other related materials shall be placed in the file of the sanctioned person.

Article 35 Where a sanctioned person is dissatisfied with a decision on disciplinary sanction, they may apply for a review to the people's court that made the decision within 30 days from the date of receipt of the decision. The court conducting the review shall make a review decision within 30 days. If still dissatisfied with the review decision, they may appeal to the people's court at the next higher level that made the review decision within 30 days of receiving the review decision. The higher-level people's court shall make a decision on the appeal within 60 days.

During the period of review or appeal, the execution of the original decision shall not be suspended.

Article 36 Where, upon review of an appeal against a decision on disciplinary sanction, the higher-level people's court considers the original decision inappropriate, or where a higher-level people's court considers the decision on disciplinary sanction made by a lower-level people's court inappropriate, it may recommend that the people's court that made the original decision modify or revoke the decision; it may also directly make a decision to modify or revoke the decision in accordance with the disciplinary sanction procedures.

The decision of the higher-level people's court shall be final.

Article 37 Where there are separate provisions on the authority and procedures for imposing disciplinary sanctions on judges, those provisions shall apply.

Article 38 Where a whistleblower intentionally fabricates facts and falsely accuses court staff, it is recommended that the relevant authorities handle the matter; if it constitutes a crime, the matter shall be transferred to the relevant authorities according to law to pursue criminal liability.

Article 39 Where a supervised unit, department, or person violates these Regulations by committing any of the following acts, the supervision department shall order correction; if correction is refused, the responsible person shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions:

(1) Concealing the true facts, producing false evidence, or concealing, transferring, tampering with, or destroying evidence;

(2) Intentionally delaying or refusing to provide documents, materials, financial accounts, or other relevant materials and necessary information related to the supervisory matter;

(3) Selling or transferring suspected property during the investigation;

(4) Refusing to make explanations or clarifications regarding questions raised by the supervision department;

(5) Refusing to execute disciplinary sanction decisions or, without justifiable reasons, refusing to adopt supervision recommendations;

(6) Other acts violating these Regulations, where the circumstances are serious.

Chapter 6 Supplementary Provisions

Article 40 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 41 These Regulations shall come into effect as of the date of issuance.
